title: Evaluation of a scheme character at an algebra-valued point
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $T$ be a $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], and let $\chi:T\to\mathbf G_m$ be a group-scheme homomorphism, with $\mathbf G_m=\operatorname{Spec}k[z,z^{-1}]$ as in [def-sc-gm-ga]. For every commutative $k$-algebra $R$ and point $t:\operatorname{Spec}R\to T$ over $k$, define the character scalar $\chi_R(t)\in R$ by pulling back the Laurent coordinate $z$ [def-weil-laurent-polynomial-ring] along $\chi\circ t$ and applying the canonical identification $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathcal O)=R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. More explicitly, it is the image of $z$ under $k[z,z^{-1}]\simeq\Gamma(\mathbf G_m,\mathcal O)\xrightarrow{(\chi\circ t)^*}\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathcal O)\simeq R$. No affineness or centrality hypothesis on $T$ is imposed.
